alt: The neutral curve in the plane of wavenumber and Rayleigh number: a U-shaped red line with its minimum marked at Ra about 1708 and k about 3.12; the region above it, where modes grow, is shaded; two crosses at k = pi mark Ra = 1500 and 2500.
caption: Rayleigh-Bénard onset between rigid plates, Pr = 1: growth rate of the least stable mode over a grid of (k, Ra), from the parametric pencil of the onset block. The red line is where it vanishes; modes grow in the shaded region. Its minimum is the critical point Ra_c = 1707.762 at k_c = 3.1163. The crosses are the two runs of the page, Ra = 1500 (stable) and 2500 (unstable) at k = π.

alt: Left: the roll amplitude on a log scale rises along a straight dashed line, then levels off. Right: the Nusselt number stays at 1, rises to a peak and settles to a constant.
caption: The simulation of the page at Ra = 2500, Pr = 1; time in thermal diffusion units d²/κ. Left: the roll amplitude grows at the rate σ = 5.543 of the leading eigenvalue (dashed line, drawn through the run at t = 0.3) until the nonlinear terms stop it. Right: the heat flux across the layer in units of conduction, Nu = 1.474 at t = 6 (it varies by 4×10⁻¹⁵ over the last time unit).

alt: A few eigenvalues in the plane of phase speed and growth, all below the zero line except one red point just above it near Re c = 0.24.
caption: Plane Poiseuille flow at Re = 10⁴, α = 1: the 7 modes kept by the drift test of the page (found again at N = 96). A mode varies as exp(iα(x − ct)), so Re c is its phase speed and α Im c its growth rate. Only the Tollmien-Schlichting wave (red), c = 0.23753 + 0.00374i, lies above the dashed line Im c = 0.

alt: The magnitudes of the 64 Chebyshev coefficients of the mode on a log scale, even indices as red dots and odd indices as open blue squares: the even ones fall from 1 to about 4×10⁻¹⁰; the odd ones stay near 3×10⁻¹⁶.
caption: The Chebyshev coefficients of the mode (mode.coeffs("v")), even and odd indices apart. v is even in y, so only the even coefficients carry it: they fall to 4×10⁻¹⁰ at the last even index. The odd ones stay at the rounding level, about 3×10⁻¹⁶. The largest of the last 10 % of the coefficients is 6×10⁻⁹ of the largest one, the spectral-tail measure that the eigenvalue result reports.

alt: The neutral curve of plane Poiseuille flow: a red tongue opening to the right in the plane of Reynolds number (log scale) and wavenumber, its nose marked at Re about 5772 and alpha about 1.02.
caption: Im c of the least stable mode on a grid of (Re, α), from the parametric pencil of the page. Inside the red line the flow is unstable. Its nose is the critical point the script finds, Re_c = 5772.2 at α_c = 1.0205.

alt: The roll amplitude on a log scale against time: the dots bend during a short start, then follow a straight red line over the shaded interval.
caption: The initial-value problem against the eigenvalue problem. Before t = 0.3 faster modes are still decaying; over the shaded interval the amplitude grows at σ = 5.5425080, the eigenvalue's 5.5425059: a relative difference of 4×10⁻⁷, within the 10⁻⁵ the script checks.

alt: Two horizontal bars over time: the upper one in two parts, job 1 then job 2, joined at a checkpoint marker at t = 0.3; the lower one a single uninterrupted run to the same end time.
caption: The jobs block of the page: job 2 resumes from the checkpoint that job 1 wrote at iteration 600 (t = 0.3) and runs to t = 0.8 (iteration 1600). Its final state is identical to that of the uninterrupted run: np.array_equal is True over the 1531 coefficients, largest difference 0. The output file holds 17 rows, t = 0 included.

alt: Three rows of eigenvalues along the growth-rate axis: open circles for the full space, red dots for the onset class, blue crosses for the other class; thin lines join each circle to the class row that holds it, and the rightmost circle, at zero, joins a red dot.
caption: The 12 eigenvalues of the full space with σ > −160, each joined to the symmetry class that holds the same value (largest relative gap 3×10⁻¹³). All are real (largest |Im σ| 1×10⁻¹⁶). The neutral mode at the onset point, σ ≈ 0, is in the onset class.

Size of each eigenproblem and wall time of its dense QZ solve, 7 timings each (median and range), from one run on AMD EPYC 9654 96-Core Processor with 2 threads (NumPy 2.5.3, SciPy 1.17.1). Halving the unknowns made the solve 5.0 times faster here; the n³ operation count bounds the saving at 8.

alt: The solution branch of the Bratu problem: u(0) rises with lambda, turns back at a red fold near lambda = 0.878 and climbs on the upper branch, the dots lying on a thin closed-form curve.
caption: The branch followed by pseudo-arclength continuation (the page's settings, run for more points), on the closed form u(0) = 2 ln cosh a. The fold, located by bisection on the tangent, is at λ_c = 0.8784576798.

Newton from u = 0 at λ = 0.3, as printed by sol.explain(): the relative residual after each iteration, 3 iterations down to 3e-14, below the declared tolerance 1e-13. The observed order log(r(k+1)/r(k)) / log(r(k)/r(k−1)) is 1.99, 2.00 (2 for quadratic convergence).

alt: Three periodic profiles over x from 0 to 22: the equilibria E1 and E2 and the travelling wave TW1.
caption: The two equilibria and the travelling wave found by Newton-Krylov-hookstep from the page's seeds.

alt: Left: Floquet multipliers of the orbit with the unit circle; a red pair lies just outside it. Right: the leading eigenvalues of E1, two red complex pairs with positive real part.
caption: Stability of the solutions. Left: the multipliers Λ of the orbit; the red pair outside the unit circle is the unstable direction, with Floquet exponent μ₁ = log|Λ|/T = 0.0332. Right: the eigenvalues λ of E1, modes growing as exp(λt); the red ones are the four with the largest real part.

loop: the last frame returns to the first (the motion is periodic)

generation.command: python docs/site/tutorial_media.py capture --out DATA --only t05 && python docs/site/tutorial_media.py render --data DATA --only t05

alt: A yellow-green curve u(x) wriggles in the upper part of the frame while, below, its history fills a red and blue space-time map from the bottom up over two periods of the orbit.
caption: The pre-periodic orbit over two periods: the state u(x) (top) and its space-time map filling up (bottom). Every frame is a time step of the orbit's flow map.

alt: The computed eigenvalues of the drum for m = 0, 1, 2 as coloured markers, each on a black tick of the squared Bessel zeros, rising with the radial index.
caption: The vibrating drum at N = 32 radial modes: the eight slowest modes of each azimuthal number m against the closed form −j²ₘ,ₙ (ticks). Over these 24 modes the largest relative error is 3×10⁻¹⁵, the level of rounding error.

alt: The spectrum of pipe flow at Re = 1000 for (m, k) = (1, 1): eigenvalues on three branches in the left half of the complex plane; the two rightmost are marked, a red dot and a blue square.
caption: Hagen-Poiseuille flow, R = 1000, (m, k) = (1, 1): the spectrum of the pipe block, modes growing as exp(st). All modes decay. The two least stable are the centre mode, s = -0.0709 − 0.8467i, and the wall mode, s = -0.0911 − 0.4691i, of Meseguer and Trefethen (2003).

alt: Two curves in the parameter plane: a red parabola of folds through the origin, and a green line of Hopf points at beta1 = 0 for beta2 < 0 that ends at the Bogdanov-Takens point at the origin.
caption: Codimension two: the fold and Hopf curves of the Bogdanov-Takens normal form, continued in (β₁, β₂). The fold curve follows β₁ = β₂²/4 through the BT point; the Hopf curve β₁ = 0 exists for β₂ < 0 and ends at the BT point.

alt: Bifurcation diagram of the Lorenz system, x against r: a black line along x = 0 that turns dashed at r = 1, where two red branches split off; they turn dashed at the Hopf points near r = 24.7, from which brass lines of cycles bend back.
caption: The equilibria of the Lorenz system and their stability, as continued by the page (solid: stable, dashed: unstable): the origin, the pitchfork at r = 1, the branches C± and their subcritical Hopf points at r = 24.736842, and the unstable cycles born there.

alt: Nested closed loops in the (x, z) plane around the point C−, small ones near it and larger ones further out.
caption: The periodic orbits of the cycle branch (orthogonal collocation, 40 intervals of degree 4) for r from 24.735 down to 22.335 (colour bar): born at the Hopf point around the equilibrium of the continued branch (cross), they grow as r decreases.

alt: A diagram of the registry: three run cards on the left, two of them outlined in red as certified, with arrows to a query box; on the right, a reproduction box reporting an identical end state and a cache box reporting that nothing was computed.
caption: The registry of the page when the script ends. Each run records its parameters and its measured error against the closed form exp(−9κt); the two certified ones (red) are what the query returns. reproduce() runs heat_k0.2 again and compares the end states: identical, largest difference 0. A repeated call with cache=True takes no step and reads the recorded state (200 steps in the original).

alt: Three panels, one per Lyapunov exponent: a grey band of running estimates over the starts narrows with time around a red mean that settles on the dashed published value.
caption: Finite-time estimates of the three exponents, averaged from the start of the measurement, over the 32 starts of the page: the band holds the middle 80 % of the starts, the red line is their mean and the dashed lines are the published values 0.906, 0 and −14.572. The panel titles give the final mean and its standard error over the starts. Time is in the units of the Lorenz equations.

alt: Successive maxima of z plotted against each other: the dots lie on a thin tent-shaped curve above a dotted diagonal.
caption: The Poincaré section dz/dt = 0 of the page: each maximum of z against the next falls on a one-dimensional cusp map, as in Lorenz's Fig. 4 of 1963.

alt: A square map of starting points coloured red or blue by the equilibrium they end on, forming interleaved spiral bands, with C+ and C- marked and a legend below.
caption: Basins of C+ (red) and C− (blue) at r = 20 for the 2304 starts of the ensemble (z₀ = 19); the rare starts still undecided at the horizon are black. The map is symmetric under (x, y) → (−x, −y).

alt: Top: two bell-shaped curves, the direct global mode peaking downstream (right) and the adjoint mode upstream (left), overlapping little. Bottom: their product, the wavemaker, a single bump centred at x = 0 with its maximum marked in red.
caption: The direct and adjoint global modes of the Ginzburg-Landau model of the page (top) and the wavemaker S(x) = |q†(x)| |q(x)| (bottom). Advection pushes the direct mode downstream and the adjoint upstream; S is largest where they overlap, the region where a local change of the model moves the eigenvalue most. Its maximum, at |x| < 3×10⁻¹⁰, equals Chomaz's closed form |χ|/√π to a relative 7×10⁻¹².

alt: Eigenvalues of the model in grey; four of them circled in red and numbered 1 to 4, each with a black cross from the decomposition of the data at its centre.
caption: Dynamic mode decomposition of a transient made of four global modes (numbered by growth rate): the DMD eigenvalues (crosses), computed from the snapshots alone, against the model's (red circles). The distances, too small to see here, are 2×10⁻¹⁴, 4×10⁻¹³, 2×10⁻¹², 5×10⁻¹³ for modes 1 to 4.

alt: The relative difference between the native model and the translated script on a log scale, falling steeply with the number of wall-normal modes down to rounding.
caption: Relative difference between the native model and the translated script after 40 SBDF2 steps, against nz. The two tau formulations of the same equations differ by an amount that falls spectrally down to rounding.

alt: Left: twelve Lyapunov exponents with error bars, the first eight between about 0.04 and -0.32, then two near -2 and two near -5.6; the first 10 sit on red ticks of the published values. Right: the first 8 enlarged, with their error bars and reference ticks.
caption: The twelve leading exponents of Kuramoto-Sivashinsky at L = 22, with their standard errors (left), and the first 8 on a finer scale (right). Red ticks mark the 10 published values (Cvitanović et al. 2010); exponents 11 to 12 have no reference. The first 8 are the entangled modes.

alt: Two histograms of angles on a log axis: the filled red one, inside the entangled modes, reaches very small angles; the blue outline, at the split after eight modes, stays well away from zero.
caption: Angles between the span of the first j covariant vectors and the rest, at each sample. Inside the entangled modes (j = 4) near-tangencies are frequent; at j = 8 the smallest angle stays away from zero over this run.

alt: A triangular matrix of probabilities: red squares among the first 8 indices and inside the pairs 9–10 and 11–12; near white across the splits between them.
caption: Domination of the Oseledets splitting: how often the local exponent i falls below j over windows of 5 time units. The first 8 modes form the leading cluster: no violation crosses the split 8 | 9. Later modes are entangled among themselves in the pairs 9–10 and 11–12, each separated from the leading cluster.

alt: Square cells of grey streamlines with red tracer paths sliding along them, from open circles to red dots.
caption: The 32 tracers of the page in the decaying Taylor-Green vortices, t = 0 to 2 (dt = 0.025): each moves along a streamline of ψ = sin x sin y (grey) and slows down as the flow decays.

alt: The tracer error against the time step on log axes, three red points close to a dashed line of slope 3.
caption: The largest tracer error against a reference path integrated to 10⁻¹³, for the three time steps of the page. Halving dt divides it by 7.7 then 7.8: observed orders 2.94 and 2.97, close to 3 in this unsteady flow.

loop: run frames, then a 0.5 s cross-fade from the last frame to the first

alt: A round grey dye blob in a channel is sheared into a long tilted streak while five yellow-green tracers glide left and right at their own heights, those on the walls moving with them.
caption: The Couette block of the page from t = 0 to 3: the dye field and the five tracers, every two time steps. The film closes its loop with a 0.5 s cross-fade: a display transition, not part of the run.
